title: Final QA, security review, automated backups + restore drill, production release, final reports
steps: SECURITY REVIEW & HARDENING (PRD §13, §22). Run a thorough security review of the whole application as an attacker would (invoke the `security-review` skill if available for a structured pass, then go further): authentication/session (passkeys, recovery, setup token, cookies, rotation, rate limits), authorization on every endpoint and form action (enumerate routes; prove deny-by-default), CSRF/origin checks, CSP and headers, input validation and output encoding (XSS in stored free text: notes, exercise names, coach messages rendered as markdown), SQL injection (raw SQL review), SSRF (none expected), secrets handling (no secrets in client bundles, logs, error records or the repo; scan git history), the AI agent surface (prompt injection via stored text, tool authorization, proposal tampering, cost abuse/rate limits), service worker/offline data exposure after sign-out, dependency audit (pnpm audit; update or justify), supply-chain basics (lockfile, pinned actions by SHA where reasonable), logging of sensitive data. Fix every real finding with tests; document the review (method, findings, fixes, residual risks) in docs/security.md.

AUTOMATED BACKUPS & RESTORE DRILL (PRD §9, §13; milestones M9 criterion 2). The Neon project is on the free plan (scheduled snapshots unavailable; 6 h point-in-time window) and GitHub Actions secrets cannot be set by the tech lead's tooling, so implement an app-level backup that needs no manual setup: a Vercel Cron job (vercel.json crons, daily, Hobby-compatible) calls a protected endpoint (verify Vercel's `Authorization: Bearer ${CRON_SECRET}` header — CRON_SECRET is an env var; document it) that exports every owner table (all application data, not sessions/challenges) as a versioned, schema-tagged JSON (streamed, gzip), encrypts it with AES-256-GCM using BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY (32-byte key from env; never logged), and uploads it to Vercel Blob (`@vercel/blob`, private access, BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN from the connected store) under backups/YYYY/MM/DD; retention: keep 30 daily + 12 monthly (prune older). Add `pnpm backup:restore <file|blob-url> --target <DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED>` that downloads, decrypts, verifies checksum + schema version, and restores into an EMPTY target database (refuses non-empty unless --force on a branch named like a scratch branch), in one transaction, idempotent IDs preserved. Keep the existing pg_dump workflow as an optional second layer (documented). Tests: unit (encryption round-trip, tamper detection, retention selection), integration (export → encrypt → restore into a fresh local DB reproduces every row and sequence; tampered file rejected). Write the restore drill procedure in docs/deployment.md with a table to record timestamps; list in your summary the env vars/infra the tech lead must create (Blob store connection, BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, CRON_SECRET).

FINAL QA & RELEASE READINESS (PRD §18, §19; milestones M9). Full regression across every PRD §19 Playwright journey on the iPhone viewport (login via the supported auth test flow; onboarding; leaving 1RMs blank; generate the week-1 baseline program; start workout; log sets/reps/RPE; rest timer; plate calculator; substitute an unavailable exercise; refresh and restore an active workout; complete workout; view history; weekly review; generate next week; multiple concurrent disciplines; coach questions and proposals) plus the PRD §18 persistence matrix (refresh mid-workout, close/reopen, temporary network loss, restore active workout, sync completed sets, no duplicates, failed sync recovery, safe offline↔online transitions) — add any missing journey, make the whole suite green on Chromium locally and structure it to run against a deployed URL (E2E_BASE_URL + test-auth disabled ⇒ read-only smoke subset) for production verification. Accessibility sweep (axe on every screen in both themes; keyboard/VoiceOver-friendly semantics), copy review (clear, consistent, no placeholder text), error-state review, empty-state review. Final docs pass: README (what it is, screenshots, quick start), architecture, all ADRs current, environment, development, testing, deployment (incl. production state), performance (latest measured numbers), design system, agent architecture, security, milestones (all complete with links to PRs). Prepare docs/reports/performance-report.md and docs/reports/design-report.md skeletons that the tech lead fills with the council results (scores, evidence, measurements, improvements, remaining issues, browser/device results).
acceptance: A documented security review covers auth/session, authorization of every route, CSRF/CSP/headers, XSS in stored text and markdown, SQL injection, secrets (bundles, logs, history), the agent surface, offline data after sign-out and dependencies; every real finding is fixed with a test; residual risks are listed.

Automated daily backups: Vercel Cron → protected endpoint → encrypted (AES-256-GCM) gzip JSON export of all owner data → private Vercel Blob with 30-daily/12-monthly retention; restore command restores into an empty database with checksum/schema verification; unit and integration tests prove export→restore fidelity and tamper rejection.

Every PRD §19 Playwright journey and the PRD §18 persistence matrix are covered and green locally on an iPhone viewport; a read-only production smoke subset runs against a deployed URL via E2E_BASE_URL.
Accessibility (axe zero violations on every screen, both themes), copy, empty and error states reviewed and fixed.

Documentation is complete and accurate (README, architecture, ADRs, environment, development, testing, deployment incl. restore drill procedure, performance with latest real numbers, design system, agent architecture, security, milestones), with report skeletons ready for the council results.
All gates pass locally (check, lint, unit, integration, both builds, budgets, full e2e incl. perf); work committed on feat/m9-release with Conventional Commits.
